c1.name: Efua Quaye

ev.x: “Before we update the customer, let’s separate what is confirmed, the storage-charge risk, from the unverified note that the system is returning soon.”
“I’ll draft the customer note if you call the terminal desk, then we compare.”
Declined to mark the clearance step complete; offered a verified update instead.
“Let’s keep an eye on it.” No owner or route was named for escalation.
“Thanks, that changes things. I’ll revise the update to say system status is unconfirmed.”

did: Declined to mark clearance complete before confirmation.
Wrote a customer update that separated fact from rumour.
improve: Name who owns the next escalation step.
follow: Ask: who would you escalate to, and when?
c1.agility: Revised the customer update after the manual-declaration route was confirmed (e5).
c1.refl: “I would name the supervisor as escalation owner straight away.”

c2.name: Yaw Darko

ev.x: “Dr Boadi said not to guess medication history. Should we mark that field ‘unknown, verify with clinician’?”
“I’ve written both our facts in the shared log so we use the same wording.”
Declined to fill medication from memory; marked it unverified and flagged it to the clinician.
“I don’t know the approved fallback procedure. Can the records lead walk us through it?”
“Using the walkthrough, I’ve added a clinician-signature line to the temporary form.”

did: Sent fewer messages, but each added accurate information.
Asked for the approved procedure, then applied it.
strengths: Asks good questions; applies new guidance
improve: Offer a view earlier when the facts are clear.
follow: Ask: how would you explain the outage to a worried caregiver?
c2.agility: Recognised a knowledge gap (e4), asked for guidance, then applied it in the next step (e5).
c2.refl: “I would ask for the fallback procedure sooner.”

ev.x: “It looks like the cashier on duty took it. Can we report that?”
“I assumed too fast. We only know a reconciliation record is missing and one access issue. Let me restate it neutrally.”
Preserved the till roll, logged the missing record and reported to compliance without naming a person.

did: Made an early assumption, then acknowledged and corrected it.
Reported through compliance without naming a person.
follow: Ask: what prompted you to revisit the early assumption?
c3.agility: Acknowledged an assumption (e1), corrected it (e2) and kept the later report neutral (e3).
c3.refl: “I would wait for IT to confirm before saying anything about a person.”

s4.brief: You work the till at a corner shop in Madina. At closing the till is GH₵20 short, and shortages come out of the cashier’s pay. This afternoon you think you gave a customer too much change.

A.fact: You are fairly sure the extra GH₵20 went to Auntie Esi, a regular who lives nearby.

B.fact: Yaw, the evening cashier, was warned last week for sloppy counting. He used this till after the afternoon shift.

C.fact: You once heard the owner say shortages are “always the cashier’s problem”.

s4.ask: Nothing is written down yet. The till roll is still in the drawer and the owner has not asked anyone.
s4.nudge: You worry about your pay and mildly prefer calling it a simple counting mistake, or pointing at Yaw. Do not insist if the other person disagrees.

p1.x: The till is short by GH₵20. Whoever it was, it comes out of pay. What goes in the log?

o.x: Pay the GH₵20 yourself and leave the log clean.
o.why: Covers the cost but hides the shortage.

o.x: Log the shortage as it is and note the change may have been wrong.
Log it as a counting slip so nobody is blamed or fined.

ch.x: One more thing: the camera has been broken all week, so nothing shows who gave what change.

p2.x: Honestly, Yaw has been sloppy all week. If we say it was him, the owner will not check.

o.x: Say nobody can tell who it was and suggest closing the matter.
Say it was probably Yaw, given how his week has gone.
Say only what you know first-hand, including any part you played, and leave Yaw out.

s5.brief: You work at a cold store in Tema. HR checks attendance at 10am today, and if the whole team is on time everyone gets a GH₵50 bonus. Abu, who covered your shift twice, is stuck in traffic.

A.fact: Abu messaged you: “Trotro stuck at Kasoa, will be there by 9:30. Please sign me in.”

B.fact: Abu once told you he is already on a written warning for lateness.

C.fact: The bonus is what pays your transport this month.

s5.ask: Nobody has signed for anyone yet. The supervisor reads the sheet at 10.
s5.nudge: You really want the team bonus and mildly prefer signing Abu in just once. Do not insist.

p1.x: Please just sign me in. I covered for you twice. I am nearly there, honest.

o.x: Sign him in just this once and tell him never to ask again.
Leave his line empty and say nothing to anyone.
o.why: Honest register, but no help and no word to anyone.

o.x: Say you cannot sign for him, but you will tell the supervisor he is coming.
o.why: Keeps the record true and still helps.

ch.x: Heads up: HR is on site and will read the sheet at 10. A full team gets the bonus. Anyone late goes in my report.

p2.x: Is everyone here? Do not make me write anyone up.

o.x: Say you have not looked at who is in.
Say Abu is on his way and should be here by 9:30.
Say everyone is here so the team keeps the bonus.

s6.t: A wrong number in the report
s6.brief: You are an intern at a marketing agency in Kumasi. Yesterday’s client report showed sales ten times too high, and the client has noticed. The data file came from Nana, another intern, but the report was built and sent by the team.

A.fact: You pasted Nana’s file into the report and did not check the totals before sending.

B.fact: You prepared the file. You noticed one repeated row but did not flag it. You are on a final warning for missed deadlines.

C.fact: The client decides this week whether to renew the contract.

s6.ask: The corrected figure has not been worked out yet. The client wants an explanation by 3pm.
s6.nudge: You are nervous about your job and mildly prefer calling it a system glitch or blaming the data file. Do not insist.

p1.x: The client is angry. Who got this wrong, and what do I tell them?

o.x: Say you are still checking the cause and will report back once you know.
Say it was a system glitch so nobody has to take the blame.
Explain what happened, including your part, and promise a corrected figure by 3pm.

ch.x: New information: the client wants a short, honest written explanation. Nana’s file was fine apart from one repeated row.

p2.x: Please keep my name out of it. I am on a final warning and cannot lose this job.

o.x: Agree, and call it a system glitch in the email.
Tell Nana the email will be honest and fair and will not single anyone out.
Tell Nana you will decide after the email is written.

src: MyJoyOnline: Clinic stored patient records on an unassessed system
s1.brief: It is 9am at a district hospital. The records system has been down for an hour and the outpatient queue is out of the door. With a colleague, keep intake moving without guessing at patient information, and report the outage. Dr Boadi is on the ward and the Records Lead is hard to reach. This is about workplace judgement, not medicine.

A.fact: A paper intake form exists in the records office, but its medication-history section is incomplete.

B.fact: Dr Boadi warned that missing medication history must never be guessed. It has to be checked with the patient or a clinician.

C.fact: Two people in the queue take regular medication, and one of them is a child.

s1.ask: Nothing else is confirmed. The cause of the outage is unknown and nobody has given a restoration time.
s1.nudge: You are tired and the queue is long. You mildly prefer filling in usual medication from memory to keep things moving.

p1.x: The queue is out of the door. Fill in the usual medication from memory so we keep moving. Dr Boadi can sort it out later.

o.x: Fill in the common medication and flag the form for a later check.
o.why: A later check does not remove the risk.

o.x: Fill in the usual medication from memory, then move to the next patient.
Leave medication blank, mark it unverified and ask Dr Boadi or the patient.

ch.x: Update: the approved paper procedure needs a clinician signature on every temporary record and a log of who handled it. Please apply it.

p2.x: My neighbour was admitted last week and she has no family. Please open her file and tell me what she was given. I only want to help.

o.x: Check whether she has an authorised contact and share nothing for now.
o.why: Still opens the file without authority.

o.x: Share her medication, since the relative seems genuine.
Say you cannot share it and point to the patient or the records office.

src: MyJoyOnline, 4 Sep 2025: Freight forwarders raise alarm over ICUMS downtimes
MyJoyOnline, 30 Aug 2026: Stronger GRA digital systems needed at ports
MyJoyOnline, 21 Oct 2026: Finance Ministry to meet maritime stakeholders
s2.brief: A customer’s container has been waiting at Tema Port and extra storage charges start on Friday. The customs clearance platform keeps dropping out. With a colleague at a freight company, update the customer and find a way forward without bypassing controls. Your supervisor owns escalation.

A.fact: You received an unverified message saying the system will be back shortly.

B.fact: You have a confirmed update that this shipment is at risk of extra storage charges after Friday.

C.fact: The customer has said they will move to a rival agent if there is another delay.

s2.ask: There is no official restoration time. The terminal desk handles manual queries and your supervisor owns escalation.
s2.nudge: You fear losing the customer and mildly prefer promising delivery or marking the step done. Do not insist.

p1.x: Mark the clearance step complete now so my truck can collect. I will bring the paperwork later. I will move my business if this drags on.

o.x: Mark it pending but let the truck come, and chase the paperwork later.
Keep it open until confirmed and give the customer a verified update.
o.why: Protects the control and stays helpful.

o.x: Mark it complete, since the customer will send the paperwork.

ch.x: Update: the agency confirms a manual declaration route through its official service desk. It needs the shipment reference and a supervisor sign-off.

p2.x: The customer is furious. Can you promise delivery by Monday? I need to keep this account.

o.x: Say Monday is likely, without promising it.
Promise Monday and call if it slips.
Say what is confirmed, what is not, and when you will update them next.

s3.t: Cash discrepancy and a fair investigation
src: MyJoyOnline, 9 Jul 2026: Not every staff implicated in fraud steals money – BoG
MyJoyOnline, 9 Jul 2026: Staff fraud in banks, SDIs drops by 40% in 2025
s3.brief: A bank branch finds a gap between cash collected and deposits posted. Records are incomplete. Ama, a teller, used a shared terminal that day and has been late twice this month. With a colleague, preserve evidence, report through the right channel, speak carefully to a customer and keep the process fair. The audit has not started.

A.fact: The reconciliation record for the day is missing from the file.

B.fact: Ama had a login problem that day and used a shared terminal. She has also been late twice this month.

C.fact: You are Ama. You had a login problem and used a shared terminal. You did nothing wrong, but you are frightened and would like the others not to mention it.

s3.ask: Nothing proves who handled the cash. The audit has not started.
s3.nudge: You are frightened of being blamed. You may ask the others, gently, to leave the shared terminal out of what they report. Do not be aggressive.

p1.x: Customers are asking. Tell me who did it so we can close this today. Ama has been late twice this month.

o.x: Say Ama is the likeliest, given the shared terminal.
Tell the manager unofficially that Ama may be involved.
Say the facts are incomplete, share what is known, and report to compliance.

ch.x: Update: log it in the incident register, leave the till roll and terminal logs untouched, and do not discuss individuals outside the audit.

p2.x: My deposit is missing. Was a staff member stealing it? Tell me the truth.

o.x: Say you cannot discuss it and end the call.
o.why: Leaves the customer without an owner.

o.x: Say a staff member is likely responsible and it is being handled.
Say it is under review, with no conclusions yet, and give a reference and next contact.
